text:
ops-oncall: Heads up — seeing ~15% pod-to-pod packet loss between GPU nodes in west-3 after this morning's Calico upgrade (3.33.0). Multiple RDMA jobs failing handshake. Any immediate ideas?

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed calico/3.33.0 rollout completed to west-3 at 08:14 UTC.

maya: same here, traces show large-frame flows (jumbo frames) get fragmented; RDMA handshake times out. Affected nodes are all gpu-pool-*.

sam: can you paste outputs from ip link / ethtool and any tcpdump/iperf?

ops-oncall: posted from gpu-node-12 — short extracts:
```
root@gpu-node-12:~# ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 1450 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
root@gpu-node-12:~# ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i gso
tx-gso: on
rx-gro: on
```
And tcpdump showing fragmentation of large UDP payloads used by RDMA probe:
```
14:02:12.123456 IP 10.0.2.5 > 10.0.2.8: UDP, length 4096
14:02:12.123457 IP (frag) 10.0.2.5 > 10.0.2.8: UDP, length 2048
14:02:12.123458 IP (frag) 10.0.2.5 > 10.0.2.8: UDP, length 2048
```

jia: Calico 3.33 introduced an "auto-MTU" behavior when encapsulation path chosen; it prefers VXLAN/IPIP and sets lower MTU (1450) to avoid outer-header fragmentation. Our on-host RDMA and NVLINK expect jumbo frames through the tunnel path — that MTU change will break RDMA. Also seeing GSO/GRO interactions with iptables CONNMARK in the Felix chains.

leo: RDMA error logs on the task: "rdma_connect: timeout waiting for response" and kernel shows skb fragmentation counts spiking.

maya: quick mitigation options: (1) explicitly set FelixConfiguration ipInIpMTU/ipinipMTU to match host jumbo MTU (8900) or (2) force Calico to use none/host-gw mode for gpu nodes. We also have FELIX_IGNOREHOSTREASONS flags we could try.

sam: I can push a configmap patch to set ipInIpMTU=8950 in calico-config and restart calico pods. Quick note: the daemonset image for 3.33 also changed startup ordering — restart may trigger kubelet race on some nodes. Proceed with canary.

ops-oncall: doing canary on 2 nodes now with ipInIpMTU=8950 applied via ConfigMap + rolling restart of calico pods.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout update: 2/6 gpu nodes patched OK.

ops-oncall: after canary, RDMA handshake succeeded on those 2 nodes, retransmits dropped to baseline. Rolling to remaining 4.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: 4/6 completed, 2 remaining — kubelet on gpu-node-18 failed to pick up new CNI config: "failed to create cni config: file exists". kubelet logs show restart spike.

maya: pause rollout. kubelet race likely due to calico configmap apply + daemonset restart ordering. If we continue we risk more node churn.

sam: rolled back calico image on remaining nodes to previous image and left configmap change in place. Confirming kubelet stable on those nodes. Planning full rollback of 3.33 -> 3.32.1 for west-3 at 03:00 UTC unless objections.

jia: agreed on rollback. Also filing follow-up: add MTU/regression tests to our node-provision CI and add a pre-upgrade check for FELIX auto-MTU changes. We should also document RDMA checklist for CNI upgrades (explicitly check ipip/vxlan MTU, host-gw fallback, and GSO/GRO offloads).

leo: opened an incident ticket and attached kernel/tcpdump logs. Adding perf counters for skb_frag and tx_retrans.

ops-oncall: thanks — will schedule a postmortem and change the upgrade runbook: 1) canary with RDMA workload, 2) explicitly set Felix MTU on gpu pools, 3) avoid rolling daemonset image + config change in same batch.

maya: fyi, long-term we should consider host-gw for GPU pools or dedicate a non-encapsulated path for RDMA traffic. But for now rollback + config fix is the safest. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll prepare the rollback PR and the emergency playbook entry.

ops-oncall: closing for now — reverting fully and will update once rollback scheduled. Thanks everyone.
